metadata.name: Lower urinary tract infection
metadata.organ_system: Urinary bladder and lower urinary tract
metadata.emergency_level: Usually outpatient; urgent if upper UTI, sepsis, obstruction or high-risk host
metadata.severity: Usually mild-moderate; potentially serious in pregnancy, men, children or complicated infection

overview.short_description: A symptomatic infection of the bladder/lower urinary tract, commonly causing dysuria, frequency and urgency without systemic upper-tract features.
overview.detailed_description: Lower UTI is diagnosed from an age-, sex- and context-appropriate symptom assessment and urine testing strategy. Fever, flank pain, rigors, vomiting, sepsis, obstruction or prostate involvement changes the pathway. Asymptomatic bacteriuria is not the same diagnosis and is generally not treated except in defined groups.
overview.pathophysiology: Usually ascending bacterial colonisation of the urethra and bladder, influenced by host anatomy, urinary stasis, instrumentation and antimicrobial exposure.
overview.etiology: Most often enteric bacteria; organism and resistance vary with prior antibiotics, healthcare exposure, catheters and local epidemiology.
overview.incubation_period: Not usefully defined for routine clinical care.
overview.natural_history: Some uncomplicated episodes resolve, but persistent infection can ascend or recur; complicated infection has higher failure risk.
overview.prognosis: Generally good with appropriate assessment and treatment; worse with obstruction, pregnancy, renal disease or systemic spread.

prevalence.value: Common in primary care, especially in women

incidence.value: Varies by age, sex and urinary risk factors

mortality.value: Very low in uncomplicated lower UTI; rises with sepsis/complication

epidemiology.age_groups: All ages; diagnostic pathways differ for children, adults and older people
epidemiology.sex_predominance: More common in people with female urinary anatomy

risk_factors.pregnancy: Changes testing, antibiotic choice and follow-up
risk_factors.medications: Recent antibiotics alter resistance; SGLT2 inhibitors and immunosuppression may change context
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Prior UTI, stones, retention, urinary abnormality, catheter or prostate disease

symptoms.symptom: Fever, rigors, flank pain or vomiting
symptoms.importance: Suggests upper/systemic infection, not uncomplicated cystitis

negative_findings.why_important: Reduces likelihood and prompts alternative causes
Vaginitis or STI becomes more likely

negative_findings.finding: No fever, flank pain, rigors or vomiting
negative_findings.why_important: Supports lower rather than upper infection

history_questions.question: Do you have burning, frequency or urgency, and when did they start?
Any fever, shaking chills, pain in the side/back, vomiting or feeling very unwell?
Could you be pregnant, and what is your age and urinary anatomy?
Any vaginal/urethral discharge, irritation, sexual exposure or pelvic pain?
Any catheter, retention, stones, prostate symptoms, kidney disease, diabetes, immunosuppression, prior cultures or recent antibiotics?

physical_examination.examination: Temperature, pulse, blood pressure and general appearance
physical_examination.expected_finding: Usually stable; systemic abnormality changes pathway
Possible suprapubic tenderness; flank tenderness suggests pyelonephritis

physical_examination.examination: Directed genital/pelvic or prostate assessment only when indicated
physical_examination.expected_finding: May identify STI, vaginitis, retention or prostatitis

vital_signs.heart_rate: Usually normal; tachycardia may indicate pain, dehydration or sepsis
vital_signs.blood_pressure: Usually normal; hypotension is a red flag
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: Usually normal; elevation may indicate sepsis/pain
vital_signs.bmi: Record when relevant to risk or treatment

laboratory_tests.indication: Support selected diagnoses; not a stand-alone universal rule
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: Men, pregnancy, children, recurrent/complicated infection, treatment failure or when pathway directs
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: When pregnancy is possible and status is unknown
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

imaging.when_needed: Not routine for simple first lower UTI; consider recurrent, atypical, obstruction/retention or paediatric pathway
imaging.expected_findings: Structural abnormality, hydronephrosis, stone or residual urine

ecg.when_needed: Not routine; use when cardiac disease, electrolyte disturbance or medicine risk indicates

other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Urine culture according to population and complication risk
other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: NAAT for STI when exposure/discharge/urethritis or cervicitis is plausible

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: An appropriate cluster of new lower urinary symptoms without upper/systemic features, interpreted through an age-, sex- and context-specific urine-testing pathway.

diagnostic_scores.value: Use the current UKHSA adult decision tools; do not apply a single rule to every population.

diagnostic_criteria.cutoff_values: No universal single culture or dipstick cutoff is authored here; use the current laboratory and guideline pathway.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Fever, flank pain, rigors, vomiting or systemic illness
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Fever, flank pain, rigors, vomiting or systemic illness

differential_diagnosis.differences: Discharge, irritation, sexual exposure or pelvic/testicular symptoms
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Discharge, irritation, sexual exposure or pelvic/testicular symptoms

differential_diagnosis.differences: Colicky flank pain, retention or hydronephrosis
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Colicky flank pain, retention or hydronephrosis
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Can you pass urine and is pain colicky?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Bladder pain syndrome or noninfectious irritation
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are symptoms persistent between supposed infections?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are there fever, rigors, flank pain or vomiting?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Any present changes urgency and antibiotic pathway

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there vaginal or urethral discharge/irritation?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Prominent discharge lowers confidence in simple UTI

next_best_question.question: Any fever/flank pain, pregnancy, male/prostate involvement, child age, catheter, retention or recent resistant culture?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Uncomplicated lower UTI versus upper/complicated pathway
next_best_question.branching_logic: High-risk or systemic features -> culture and urgent/specialist pathway; otherwise use lower-UTI decision tool

next_best_test.why: Testing depends on age, sex, pregnancy and complication risk
next_best_test.expected_outcome: Supports diagnosis and guides narrow therapy

red_flags.finding: Fever/rigors, flank pain, vomiting or sepsis physiology
Urinary retention, anuria or suspected infected obstruction
Pregnancy with systemic illness or infant under 3 months with suspected UTI
Failure to improve within 48 hours or rapid worsening
red_flags.immediate_action: Reassess diagnosis, culture, resistance and complications

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Upper/systemic features, pregnancy with complication, high-risk child, obstruction/retention or significant comorbidity.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Recurrent/persistent UTI, haematuria after infection resolves, suspected structural dysfunction.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Sepsis, infected obstruction, anuria or haemodynamic instability.

late: Renal injury in selected complicated/paediatric cases

initial_management.supportive_care: Assess population and complication risk, obtain urine sample when indicated, provide symptom care and safety-netting.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Paracetamol; Nitrofurantoin; Trimethoprim; Culture- and group-directed beta-lactam; Fosfomycin. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: UKHSA_UTI_DIAG_2025, NICE_NG109_2025, NICE_NG224.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Maintain hydration; avoid delayed care for systemic symptoms.
initial_management.follow_up: Review culture when sent and reassess if worsening or not improving within 48 hours.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Population-, culture- and local-resistance-directed lower-UTI antibiotic; never use nitrofurantoin for suspected upper infection.

patient_education.home_advice: Burning and frequent urination may be a bladder infection, but fever, shaking, side/back pain, vomiting or inability to pass urine can mean a more serious infection and need urgent care.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: قد يدل الحرقان وكثرة التبول على التهاب المثانة، لكن الحمى أو الرجفة أو ألم الخاصرة/الظهر أو القيء أو عدم القدرة على التبول قد تعني التهاباً أخطر وتحتاج تقييماً عاجلاً.
patient_education.prevention: Avoid unnecessary antibiotics; investigate recurrent infection rather than repeatedly self-treating.
patient_education.warning_signs: Fever, flank pain, vomiting, confusion, pregnancy with worsening symptoms, retention or no improvement within 48 hours.

prevention.lifestyle: Hydration and addressing retention/catheters or other individual risk factors
prevention.screening: Do not screen/treat asymptomatic bacteriuria routinely outside guideline-defined groups

evidence.evidence_level: Guideline-grounded direction; no claim that every narrative sentence has clinician verification.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by UKHSA_UTI_DIAG_2025, NICE_NG109_2025, NICE_NG224; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

limitations: Guidelines require individual clinical judgement and may differ by country, formulary and antimicrobial resistance.
The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Confirm likely lower UTI, distinguish upper/complicated infection and use the narrowest effective culture- and population-appropriate antibiotic.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Paracetamol; Nitrofurantoin; Trimethoprim; Culture- and group-directed beta-lactam; Fosfomycin. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: UKHSA_UTI_DIAG_2025, NICE_NG109_2025, NICE_NG224.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Hydration to avoid dehydration, symptom relief and clear safety-netting; do not treat asymptomatic bacteriuria except guideline-defined groups such as pregnancy.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Pain or fever while diagnostic and antibiotic decisions are made
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: severe active liver disease or prior serious reaction
use_caution_if: heavy alcohol use, malnutrition, low body weight, or concomitant paracetamol-containing products
monitoring: total daily exposure and clinical response

medication_options.role: first-choice lower-UTI antibiotic in eligible groups
medication_options.when_to_consider: Only for lower UTI after renal, pregnancy, upper-UTI and prostate-involvement review
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: suspected pyelonephritis/systemic infection, significant renal impairment below the current product threshold, previous nitrofurantoin lung/liver injury, or serious allergy
use_caution_if: pregnancy near term, G6PD deficiency, anaemia, pulmonary or hepatic disease, peripheral neuropathy, older/frail patient, or repeated/prolonged courses
monitoring: clinical response, renal eligibility, and pulmonary/hepatic/neurological symptoms; reassess promptly if systemic symptoms develop

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only when resistance risk/culture, pregnancy, renal function and interactions permit
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: serious trimethoprim allergy, severe folate-deficiency blood disorder, or pregnancy when contraindicated by the selected product/local guideline
use_caution_if: renal impairment, hyperkalaemia risk, folate deficiency, older/frail patient, or ACE inhibitor/ARB/MRA/potassium/methotrexate interaction
monitoring: clinical response; potassium, renal function and blood count when risk or duration warrants

medication_options.when_to_consider: Pregnancy, children, men or resistant infection according to culture and current local guidance
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: documented immediate or severe delayed penicillin allergy
use_caution_if: renal impairment, prior C. difficile, or recent antibiotic exposure
monitoring: clinical response, allergy and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea

avoid_if: previous serious cephalosporin reaction; avoid selected beta-lactam if cross-reactive severe allergy risk is unacceptable
use_caution_if: renal impairment, prior severe penicillin reaction, previous C. difficile, recent antibiotics, or seizure risk with selected high-dose agents
monitoring: clinical response, allergy, renal-adjusted dosing and antibiotic-associated diarrhoea

medication_options.when_to_consider: When listed by the current local pathway and upper/systemic infection has been excluded
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: serious fosfomycin reaction or use for suspected upper/systemic UTI where adequate renal-tissue treatment is required
use_caution_if: significant renal impairment, pregnancy, recurrent/complicated infection, or high sodium load for selected IV formulations
monitoring: clinical response, gastrointestinal adverse effects and culture-directed reassessment

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent assessment for sepsis, pyelonephritis, pregnancy with systemic illness, urinary obstruction/retention, very young infant, immunocompromise or failure to improve within 48 hours.
